name: Uploading sheets and BIM models
summary: Adding 2D sheets and BIM models to a project location, choosing their sheet or BIM type, naming them, and the access rules around design uploads.

roles.note: The server picks the sheet or BIM permission itself: on create it checks create-project-design when the request type is "Plan Drawings" (which the web sends for every sheet) and create-project-bim otherwise; on update and delete it uses the stored category. The grants reflect intended design from role naming (SRC-004), not deployed role data.

requirements.title: Supported design file types
requirements.statement: Users can upload sheets as PDF, DWG or DXF and BIM models as RVT or NWD. Whether DXF should stay supported, and whether other formats are needed, is open in the PRDs.
requirements.rationale: The web upload accepts exactly these five extensions. The stored format list also allows IFC, SKP, SVF and SVF2, which the web doesn't offer for upload.

requirements.title: Every design is a sheet or a BIM model, and a sheet has a sheet type
requirements.statement: A design is either a BIM model or a sheet. A sheet takes its type from one of the project's sheet types; if none is given it is stored as a generic drawing. The Architectural Sheet type is stored under the legacy name "Plan Drawings".

requirements.title: Built-in sheet and BIM types, with Architectural Sheet locked
requirements.statement: Every new project starts with seven sheet types (Architectural, Electrical, Fire Safety, Plumbing Drainage, Plumbing Domestic, Cable Tray and Mechanical) and one BIM type. Architectural Sheet and the BIM type can't be rearranged, renamed, recoloured or deleted, and no sheet type can be swapped into Architectural Sheet when another type is deleted.
requirements.rationale: General option rules (unique names, locked options, in-use options) are in PROJ-REQ-026..028.

requirements.title: Who may upload and edit designs
requirements.statement: Only project admins may add, edit or delete sheets and BIM models. Collaborators and viewers can view and download them.
requirements.rationale: The role matrix and permission seed give design and BIM write permissions to admins only. The PRDs disagree with each other: one has collaborators cropping and tagging PDF pages, another has collaborators only viewing.

dispute.summary: The document-management PRD (US-002) has a collaborator cropping and tagging PDF pages for designs. The hierarchy-design PRD (US-006) says a collaborator only views structures "without making changes". The current role matrix denies collaborators create, update and delete on designs and BIM. See DEC-040.

requirements.title: How many BIM models a project may have
requirements.statement: A project may hold several BIM models and several sheets for each location, and users can switch between them when viewing.
requirements.rationale: The hierarchy-management PRD asks for multiple BIMs and sheets per level. The web treats BIM as "meant to be uploaded once per project" and warns, without blocking, when any BIM already exists anywhere in the project.

dispute.summary: PRD FR-006 and US-003 want multiple BIM models per project and per level. The web's duplicate check says BIM is meant to be uploaded once per project and shows a non-blocking warning when one already exists, or when the file's checksum matches an existing BIM. See DEC-044.

requirements.title: A design's display name is separate from its file name
requirements.statement: Users can rename a design after upload. The platform and legend show the display name instead of the original file name. Renaming keeps the original file extension.

requirements.statement: Users can change a sheet's type from a dialog after upload. The same tag can't be given to two sheets; existing duplicate tags get a number appended.

requirements.title: A cropped sheet keeps its original PDF
requirements.statement: When a user crops a PDF page before upload, both the cropped sheet and the original file are stored. Tasks are not auto-imported from an integration for a cropped sheet.

requirements.title: Internal designs are hidden from customers
requirements.statement: A design is internal only when the upload explicitly marks it so. Customers don't see internal designs in lists and get "not found" when opening one; support users see them.
requirements.rationale: Counts and status chips follow the same rule (PROJ-REQ-025). The server doesn't check that the person marking a design internal is a support user.
